title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court and the China Insurance Regulatory Commission on Comprehensively Advancing the Construction of a Mechanism for Connecting Litigation and Mediation in Insurance Disputes
keywords_en: Committee on Comprehensively Advancing Insurance Disputes
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, China Insurance Regulatory Commission

Opinions on Comprehensively Advancing the Construction of a Mechanism for Docking Litigation and Mediation in Insurance Disputes

Fa [2016] No. 374

The development of a mechanism for the docking of litigation and mediation (hereinafter referred to as the "litigation-mediation docking mechanism") in insurance disputes is an important measure to implement the spirit of the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China and the Third, Fourth, Fifth, and Sixth Plenary Sessions of the 18th Central Committee, to improve the diversified dispute resolution mechanism, and to promote the modernization of social governance. Since the Supreme People's Court and the China Insurance Regulatory Commission jointly issued the "Notice on Carrying out Pilot Work on Establishing a Mechanism for Docking Litigation and Mediation in Insurance Disputes in Selected Regions Nationwide" (Fa [2012] No. 307) in 2012, the people's courts and insurance regulatory authorities in the pilot areas have strengthened coordinated operations, played an active role in preventing and resolving social conflicts, promoted the lawful, fair, and efficient resolution of insurance disputes, effectively safeguarded the legitimate rights and interests of all parties, and successfully completed all pilot tasks. In order to implement the spirit of the "Decision of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China on Major Issues Concerning Comprehensively Advancing the Rule of Law" (Zhong Fa [2014] No. 10) concerning the improvement of the diversified dispute resolution mechanism and the "Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Further Deepening the Reform of the Diversified Dispute Resolution Mechanism by the People's Courts" (Fa Fa [2016] No. 14), the following opinions are hereby put forward on further advancing the construction of the litigation-mediation docking mechanism for insurance disputes:

I. Overall Requirements

(1) Guiding Ideology

Comprehensively implement the spirit of the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China and the Third, Fourth, Fifth, and Sixth Plenary Sessions of the 18th Central Committee, take Deng Xiaoping Theory, the important thought of the "Three Represents," and the Scientific Outlook on Development as guidance, thoroughly implement the spirit of General Secretary Xi Jinping's series of important speeches, closely focus on the coordinated advancement of the "Four Comprehensives" strategic layout and the "Five Development Concepts," earnestly implement the requirements of the Party Central Committee and the State Council on improving the diversified mechanism for resolving conflicts and disputes, give full play to the active role of the people's courts, insurance regulatory authorities, and insurance industry organizations in preventing and resolving social conflicts and disputes, resolve insurance disputes lawfully, fairly, and efficiently, continuously improve the credibility of mediation, and provide convenient, efficient, and low-cost dispute resolution channels for parties to insurance disputes.

(2) Basic Principles

First, adhere to lawfulness and fairness. The work of docking litigation and mediation for insurance disputes shall be conducted lawfully and fairly, strictly abide by the procedures prescribed by laws, administrative regulations, and judicial interpretations, shall not harm the legitimate rights and interests of the parties or other interested persons, shall not violate the basic principles of the law, and shall not harm the public interest. Second, adhere to the voluntariness of mediation. The conduct of litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes must fully respect the will of all parties, shall not force mediation, and ensure that the parties exercise their civil rights and litigation rights according to law. Third, adhere to efficiency and convenience for the people. The conduct of litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes should focus on work efficiency, flexibly determine mediation methods based on the actual circumstances of the dispute, fully utilize information technology, and facilitate the parties as much as possible.

(3) Objectives and Tasks

1. Establish a sound diversified resolution mechanism for insurance disputes, provide parties to insurance disputes with more optional dispute resolution channels, achieve a sound litigation-mediation docking system, smooth operation mechanisms, standardized management of mediation organizations, lawful and fair mediation procedures, a professional and stable mediation team, and resolve conflicts and disputes lawfully, fairly, and efficiently, effectively protecting the legitimate rights and interests of all parties.

2. Actively expand the scope of regions where the mechanism is implemented. In addition to the continued conduct of litigation-mediation docking work in the previous pilot areas, the litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes shall be extended to all municipalities directly under the Central Government and provincial capital cities (capitals of autonomous regions). The higher people's courts and insurance regulatory authorities of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, based on the principle of being proactive and prudent, timely extend the litigation-mediation docking mechanism for insurance disputes to areas where there is a need for dispute resolution and where the work foundation is relatively good.

II. Strengthening Platform Construction

(4) Improving Platform Setup

Courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented shall integrate the construction of the litigation-mediation docking platform for insurance disputes with the construction of the litigation service center. Where conditions permit, they shall actively establish mediation rooms for insurance disputes for the use of specially invited mediation organizations and specially invited mediators. They shall establish a roster of specially invited mediation organizations and a roster of specially invited mediators to provide complete and accurate information on mediation organizations and mediators to parties in insurance disputes for their voluntary choice. Insurance regulatory authorities shall, in light of the actual circumstances of their jurisdiction, guide local insurance industry associations to establish and improve mediation organizations for insurance disputes. Where conditions permit, third-party mediation organizations for insurance disputes may be established to promote the standardization and normalization of mediation organizations. Insurance industry associations shall submit the list of local mediation organizations and mediators for insurance disputes to the local insurance regulatory bureau or branch for record, and the insurance regulatory bureau or branch shall provide it to the corresponding court to establish a roster of mediation organizations and mediators within its jurisdiction.

(5) Standardizing the Construction of Mediation Organizations

Insurance industry associations shall formulate management systems for mediation organizations and establish evaluation mechanisms for mediation organizations; raise and manage the operating funds of mediation organizations, formulate fund usage norms and fee payment standards; guide mediation organizations to formulate and improve the mediation rules, file management, statistical reporting, and other systems of the mediation organizations, strengthen the hardware and software construction of mediation organizations, and achieve the standardization and normalization of mediation organizations.

(6) Strengthening the Construction of the Mediator Team

Mediation organizations shall establish and improve systems for the selection, certification, training, assessment, rewards and punishments, and withdrawal of mediators; select personnel who are professionally proficient and experienced to be specifically responsible for the organization and implementation of mediation work; establish a mediation expert database, and organize relevant professionals to provide guidance for specific dispute mediation work; incorporate mediator training into the annual work plan to improve the professional ethics, legal knowledge, insurance knowledge, and mediation skills of mediators. Courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented shall strengthen guidance to mediators, and train mediators through activities such as observing court trials and conducting legal knowledge lectures to promote the continuous conduct of the litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes.

(7) Actively Promoting the Establishment of a "One-Stop" Dispute Resolution Model

Courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented and mediation organizations for insurance disputes shall actively promote and guide the establishment of a "one-stop" dispute resolution model in areas such as traffic accident dispute handling and medical dispute handling, promote the rapid resolution of disputes, and effectively reduce the burden on the parties.

III. Standardizing Operational Procedures

(8) Clarifying the Scope of Cases

Courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented shall conduct the litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes in an orderly manner in accordance with the relevant provisions of the "Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Establishing and Improving the Mechanism for Docking Litigation and Non-Litigation Dispute Resolution" (Fa Fa [2009] No. 45) and the "Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Further Deepening the Reform of the Diversified Dispute Resolution Mechanism by the People's Courts." The scope of cases for the litigation-mediation docking of insurance disputes is the insurance disputes stipulated in the "Provisions on Causes of Civil Action" of the Supreme People's Court (Fa [2011] No. 41) and other civil and commercial disputes related to insurance. Areas where the mechanism is implemented may carry out litigation-mediation docking work within the scope of the above-mentioned disputes as circumstances warrant.

(9) Improving the Docking Process for Mediation Assigned Before Case Registration

1. Pre-litigation guidance. After receiving a complaint or an oral complaint for an insurance dispute but before registering the case, the case filing department of the people's court shall guide the parties to choose mediation to resolve the dispute. If the parties agree to pre-litigation mediation, they shall fill in and sign a "Pre-Registration (Pre-Litigation) Mediation Application" or the like, or the people's court shall issue documents such as the "Pre-Registration (Pre-Litigation) Mediation Proposal" or "Pre-Registration (Pre-Litigation) Mediation Confirmation" to the parties, which shall be signed by the parties for confirmation. If the parties expressly indicate that they do not agree to mediation, the people's court shall register the case according to law.

2. Assignment of mediation. The people's court shall send a letter assigning mediation before case registration and relevant materials to the mediation organization for insurance disputes.

3. Organization of mediation. The mediator shall conduct mediation work according to law in accordance with the mediation procedures. If both parties reach an agreement, the mediation organization shall prepare a mediation agreement, which shall be signed by the mediator and both parties for confirmation. If mediation fails, the mediation organization shall promptly reply to the people's court by letter. If the parties apply for case registration, the people's court shall register the case according to law.

4. Judicial confirmation. If a party applies for judicial confirmation of the mediation agreement, the people's court shall promptly review the mediation agreement in accordance with the "Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Establishing and Improving the Mechanism for Docking Litigation and Non-Litigation Dispute Resolution," the "Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Further Deepening the Reform of the Diversified Dispute Resolution Mechanism by the People's Courts," and the relevant provisions of the Civil Procedure Law, and confirm the validity of the mediation agreement according to law.

(10) Improving the Docking Process for Mediation Referred After Case Registration

1. Referral of mediation. Where an insurance dispute has already been registered, a court in an area where the mechanism is implemented may, based on the circumstances of the case and with the consent of both parties, refer the case to a mediation organization for insurance disputes for mediation. The people's court shall issue a letter of referral for mediation, stating the referring court and the presiding judge, the parties, the cause of action, and a brief description of the case, and shall transfer the materials such as the complaint, the statement of defense, copies of the main evidence materials, and a list along with the case to the mediation organization.

2. Organization of mediation. The mediator shall conduct mediation work according to law in accordance with the mediation procedures. If both parties reach an agreement, the mediation organization shall prepare a mediation agreement, which shall be signed by the mediator and both parties for confirmation. The mediation organization shall promptly report the mediation result and relevant documents in writing to the referring court. The people's court shall, after review according to law, issue a civil mediation document. If mediation fails, the hearing of the insurance dispute case shall be resumed promptly.

(11) Strictly Adhering to Mediation Time Limits

For insurance dispute cases assigned or referred by the people's court for mediation, the mediation organization shall complete mediation within twenty working days from the date of acceptance of the case (excluding time for disability assessment, loss assessment, etc.). With the consent of both parties, the period may be appropriately extended, but the extension shall not exceed seven working days at most.

IV. Improving Working Mechanisms

(12) Establishing a Multi-Level Communication and Liaison Mechanism for the Litigation-Mediation Docking of Insurance Disputes

The courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented, insurance regulatory authorities, and other relevant parties shall regularly hold joint meetings on the litigation-mediation docking of insurance disputes to communicate on work situations, coordinate the mediation of major and typical insurance dispute cases, and promote the in-depth and effective conduct of the litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes. The courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented, insurance regulatory authorities, and mediation organizations for insurance disputes shall strengthen daily communication and liaison, promptly coordinate specific issues encountered in the litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes, and improve work quality and efficiency.

(13) Establishing an Information Sharing Mechanism for the Litigation-Mediation Docking of Insurance Disputes

Courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented, insurance regulatory authorities, and mediation organizations for insurance disputes shall improve the statistical summary system for work information and data on the litigation-mediation docking of insurance disputes, and regularly exchange information and data. For common issues in insurance disputes found during adjudication, the people's court shall issue judicial suggestions to the insurance regulatory authorities and insurance industry associations.

(14) Establishing a Guidance Mechanism for Difficult Disputes

Mediation organizations for insurance disputes may seek advice from the people's court on difficult issues encountered in mediating insurance disputes and questions concerning the application of law involved, and the people's court shall promptly provide guidance and replies.

(15) Exploring the Establishment of an Online Mediation Mechanism

Courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented and mediation organizations for insurance disputes shall actively leverage the supporting role of information technology means for the construction of the litigation-mediation docking mechanism, rely on the internet to explore the establishment of an online mediation model for insurance disputes, and promote the information-based development of the litigation-mediation docking mechanism for insurance disputes.

V. Strengthening Measures and Guarantees

(16) Strengthening Organizational Leadership

Courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented and insurance regulatory authorities shall increase their leadership and guidance over the litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes, and jointly formulate detailed rules for the litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes based on the specific actual circumstances. The higher people's courts and intermediate people's courts in the jurisdictions where the courts implementing the mechanism are located shall guide and supervise the litigation-mediation docking work within their jurisdictions and promote the smooth conduct of the litigation-mediation docking work. Courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented shall designate one division to be uniformly responsible for the external coordination of the litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes, and all relevant divisions shall actively participate in and cooperate with the litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes, paying attention to communication and collaboration. Insurance regulatory authorities shall strengthen guidance and supervision over mediation organizations, encourage insurance companies to establish mechanisms such as dynamic granting of mediation authority, remote authorization, prompt response to mediation, and rapid approval, to ensure that grass-roots branches can resolve insurance disputes through mediation. Insurance industry associations shall urge insurance companies at all levels to actively participate in mediation and promptly perform mediation agreements by organizing member companies to sign industry self-regulatory conventions. Courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented, insurance regulatory authorities, and insurance industry associations may commend and publicize collectives and individuals who have performed outstandingly in the litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes.

(17) Ensuring Sources of Funding

Courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented and insurance regulatory authorities shall actively seek support from local party committees and governments for the litigation-mediation docking work for insurance disputes, and incorporate the litigation-mediation docking work into the scope of funding guarantees for the local diversified resolution of conflicts and disputes. Insurance industry associations are encouraged to implement funding guarantees for the litigation-mediation docking mechanism in accordance with the law, such as by increasing special membership dues or collecting fees based on the number of mediation cases handled by each member company, to ensure the effective conduct of the litigation-mediation docking work.

(18) Improving the Judicial Confirmation Procedure

Where a mediation agreement with the nature of a civil contract is reached under the auspices of a mediation organization for insurance disputes, a party may apply to the primary people's court or the people's tribunal in the locality of the mediation organization for confirmation of its validity according to law. For an agreement reached through mediation assigned by a court before case registration to a mediation organization for insurance disputes, if a party applies for judicial confirmation, the primary people's court in the locality of the mediation organization or the court that assigned the mediation shall have jurisdiction.

VI. Strengthening Policy Guidance and Publicity Education

(19) Emphasizing Policy Guidance

Courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented, insurance regulatory authorities, and insurance industry associations shall actively guide parties to resolve conflicts and disputes through mediation. The people's court shall inform the parties of the relevant circumstances of the litigation-mediation docking of insurance disputes. Insurance regulatory authorities and insurance industry associations shall urge insurance companies to add content regarding the resolution of disputes through mediation in insurance application tips, claims notification letters, complaint handling notification letters, and insurance contracts. Insurance regulatory authorities shall add content regarding the resolution of disputes through mediation in complaint handling notification letters.

(20) Emphasizing Publicity and Education

Courts in areas where the mechanism is implemented, insurance regulatory authorities, and insurance industry associations shall increase publicity efforts. The people's court shall incorporate the litigation-mediation docking of insurance disputes into the legal publicity activity system. Insurance regulatory authorities and insurance industry associations shall incorporate the litigation-mediation docking mechanism for insurance disputes into the consumer education system, enhance the awareness and trust of parties in insurance disputes and the public in the litigation-mediation docking mechanism for insurance disputes, increase public participation in the litigation-mediation docking work, and form a favorable atmosphere conducive to advancing the litigation-mediation docking work.

November 4, 2016
